Provider: Dr. Jennifer Walsh, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden onset of paralysis in her left arm upon waking this morning.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 25-year-old with Gilbert syndrome and prior neurology and psychiatry encounters reports that she was unable to move her arm when she woke up this morning. She denies any pain, trauma, or previous similar episodes.

She has been under significant stress at work and recently went through a breakup.

A complete blood count, basic metabolic panel, and thyroid function tests are within normal limits.

IMAGING:
An MRI of the brain and cervical spine are unremarkable.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Chen, MD
Department: Psychiatry
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Low energy, difficulty concentrating, and increased tearfulness that began about a month ago following a breakup.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 24-year-old female with a history of Gilbert syndrome and prior psychiatric evaluation for disturbed sleep with vivid nightmares returns to the clinic with low energy, difficulty concentrating, and increased tearfulness. She reports feeling emotionally "off" since breaking up with her partner of three years. She says the breakup was amicable but unexpected, and since then, she has found herself ruminating over what went wrong and questioning her own worth. She recently started a new job at a design firm and worries that her emotional state is beginning to affect her performance. She describes herself as feeling "flat," with diminished interest in going out with friends, though she continues to go to work and complete her basic responsibilities at home. She sleeps about six hours per night and has a normal appetite. She denies suicidal thoughts, anhedonia, or feelings of hopelessness. She states, "I know it's only been a few weeks, but I just don't feel like myself."

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Gilbert syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Nightmare Disorder (diagnosed 2021-01-15)

She has never had prior episodes like this and has no personal or family history of psychiatric illness. She has not tried any medications or therapy before.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- None

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
She has never had prior episodes like this and has no personal or family history of psychiatric illness.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She does not use drugs or alcohol.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On mental status exam, she is attentive, cooperative, and oriented. Her affect is sad and constricted, and her speech is slow but coherent. There are no signs of hallucinations, delusions, or disorganized thought processes. She expresses insight into her emotional state and says she would be open to counseling.

She reports yellowing of the eyes first noticed while brushing her teeth two days ago. She recently returned home after completing a week-long religious fast during which she limited herself to only water and small portions of food once daily. She says she feels tired, but attributes this to resuming classes and preparing for final exams at her university. She denies abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dark urine, or changes in her bowel habits. Her appetite has improved since ending the fast, and she has had regular bowel movements. She reports having experienced a similar episode of "yellow eyes" once before after recovering from a mild viral illness in high school, but never sought medical attention as the discoloration resolved within days.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
She drinks alcohol only occasionally

VITAL SIGNS:

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Kim, MD
Department: Psychiatry
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Two-month history of disturbed sleep with vivid, distressing nightmares occurring several times weekly.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 23-year-old female with a known history of Gilbert syndrome, previously evaluated in Gastroenterology in January and April 2020 for intermittent scleral icterus, who presents with a two-month history of disturbed sleep. She reports that several times a week she wakes suddenly during the night from vivid, distressing dreams in which she is being chased or threatened. In the dreams, she often finds herself unable to move quickly, feeling as if her legs are weighed down, until the fear becomes so intense that she wakes up. After waking, she feels alert and remembers the dream clearly but finds it difficult to fall back asleep. She has begun drinking a glass of wine a few nights a week in an attempt to relax and get back to sleep. Over the past few weeks, she has noticed increasing daytime fatigue, irritability, and difficulty concentrating on her coursework. ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-07-15
Provider: Dr. Amara Okafor, MD
Department: Neurology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Several days of tingling and aching pain in the right leg that began after starting long evening walks in new tight running shoes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 24-year-old female with Gilbert syndrome and prior psychiatric treatment for nightmare disorder and adjustment disorder who presents with right leg symptoms. She reports that the symptoms began after she started taking long evening walks in new running shoes that feel tighter than her previous pair. She describes a burning pain along the outer aspect of her right lower leg and top of her foot, which worsens with prolonged walking. She denies any recent trauma, falls, or back pain. She has also felt more fatigued lately due to final exams, eating poorly, and sleeping only 4–5 hours per night.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Gilbert syndrome (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Nightmare Disorder (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (diagnosed 2022-01-15)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- None

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal uncle with Gilbert syndrome
- Father with benign recurrent jaundice
- No family history of psychiatric illness
- No family history of neurologic disorders

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional social use (1-2 standard drinks per week), rarely consumes wine in evenings. Occupation: Junior graphic designer at a branding firm; part-time university student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, she has mild tenderness to palpation over the lateral compartment of the leg. There is slightly reduced strength with foot eversion, but dorsiflexion and toe extension remain normal. Her gait is unaffected, and she does not demonstrate foot drop. Sensory testing reveals decreased sensation over the anterolateral shin and dorsum of the foot, excluding the web space between the first and second toes. Passive ankle inversion reproduces the tingling sensation. There is no calf tenderness or swelling, and pulses are symmetric bilaterally. Tinel’s sign is positive when tapping just anterior to the fibula. The rest of the neurologic exam is unremarkable.

PLAN:
She is advised to rest, switch to wider shoes, and take NSAIDs as needed.
